The attacker could also have seen requests being processed on that server that day, including requests sent in confidential mode, the company said earlier this week. That mode processes requests inside a trusted execution environment (TEE
items.summary: An attacker exploited an RCE flaw in the SGLang inference engine and compromised a NEAR AI server. AI developers and infrastructure teams using SGLang are affected. No fix yet: watch for a patch.

items.title: Hackers exploit trusted AWS access to breach multiple cloud environments

items.snippet: Prototype pollution via Schema.prototype.virtual() — the 2022 fix for CVE-2022-2564 / CVE-2022-24304 protected Schema.path()/add() but never virtual(), so the same class of bug is still exploitable in all maintained release lines. In lib/schema.js, Schema.prototype.virtual() (defined at line 2643) builds the virtual path via: ```javascript virtuals[name] = parts.reduce(function(mem, part, i) { me…
items.summary: Mongoose contains a prototype pollution vulnerability via Schema.prototype.virtual() affecting all maintained release lines. Upgrade mongoose to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, 9.11.4 or later.

items.title: Forge: Ed25519 signature verification accepts small-order public keys
items.snippet: `ed25519.verify()` does not reject public keys of small order, such as the identity point. Under such a key, a signature with `S = 0` and a small-order `R` verifies for many messages, or for every message with the identity key, without any private key. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.3. `crypto_sign_open()` in `lib/ed25519.js` decodes the public key `A` with `unpackneg()`, which only checks that the poin…
items.summary: Node-forge Ed25519 signature verification accepts small-order public keys, allowing forgery for certain messages. This affects developers using the node-forge library. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.3 or later.

items.title: Forge: TLS client crash on an unsupported ServerHello compression method
items.snippet: A `forge.tls` client accepts any compression method in the ServerHello, although it only offers no compression. An unknown method makes `connection.process()` throw an uncaught `Error` when the client handles ServerHelloDone, before the server is authenticated. A malicious server or an on-path attacker can use this to terminate a Node.js process. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.3. The client's ClientHell…
items.summary: A forge.tls client crash occurs on an unsupported ServerHello compression method, potentially causing a denial of service. This affects developers using node-forge for TLS clients. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.3 or later.

items.title: Forge: ReDoS in forge.http response header and cookie trimming
items.snippet: `forge.http` trims response header and `Set-Cookie` values with the regular expression `/\s*$/`, which takes quadratic time on a long run of whitespace followed by another character. A server or on-path attacker can block a `forge.http` client for minutes with one large response header. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.3. `_trimString()` in `lib/http.js` removes trailing whitespace with `str.replace(/\s*$…
items.summary: A ReDoS vulnerability in forge.http response header and cookie trimming causes quadratic CPU consumption. This affects developers parsing HTTP responses with node-forge. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.3 or later.

items.title: Forge: TLS client crash on a handshake record received without a session
items.snippet: A `forge.tls` client throws an uncaught `TypeError` from `connection.process()` when it receives a ServerHello while it has no session: after a `close_notify` alert or a call to `close()`, or before `handshake()` is called. A malicious server or an on-path attacker can use this to terminate a Node.js process. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.3. `tls.handleHandshake()` in `lib/tls.js` updates the handshake…
items.summary: A forge.tls client crash occurs on a handshake record received without an active session, terminating the Node.js process. This affects developers using node-forge TLS clients. Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.3 or later.

items.title: Mongoose: Discriminator key values matching inherited properties (e.g. __t: 'constructor') bypass schema casting and can poison collections
items.snippet: Mongoose chooses which discriminator model or schema to use by looking up the discriminator key value (`t` by default) in a plain object of registered discriminators, for example `Model.discriminators[doc.t]`. That value comes from user documents and query filters. Because the lookup did not check own properties, a value that names a property inherited from `Object.prototype` resolves to that inh…
items.summary: Mongoose discriminator key values matching inherited properties bypass schema casting and can poison collections. This affects developers using Mongoose in Node.js applications. Upgrade mongoose to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, 9.11.4 or later.

items.title: Mongoose walks into inherited properties when hydrating, setting, and merging, allowing overwrites of built-in functions (denial of service) and shared schema state
items.snippet: Three Mongoose code paths copy data into objects by property name without checking whether the property is the object's own or inherited from its prototype: 1. Loading a document from the database (`init()`, also used by `Model.hydrate()`) 2. Setting a dotted path on a document (`$__set`, used by `new Model(obj)`, `doc.set()` and `doc.$set()`) 3. Merging update documents (`utils.mergeClone`, used…
items.summary: Mongoose property handling allows overwriting built-in functions and shared schema state via inherited properties during data hydration and setting. This affects developers using Mongoose. Upgrade mongoose to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, 9.11.4 or later.

items.title: compose-lint: File paths embedded in pull requests can inject CI workflow commands through command-line error messages
items.snippet: 0.31.0 fixed GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, where text from a Compose file became GitHub Actions workflow commands in compose-lint's output. The fix escapes the command openers in compose-lint's own output, but not in the argument parser's error messages. When a repository path reaches compose-lint's arguments without a `--` before it, the argument parser prints it raw in its error message. That includes a…
items.summary: Compose-lint allows file paths in pull requests to inject CI workflow commands through argument parser error messages. Upgrade compose-lint to 0.32.0 or later.

items.title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can issue CI workflow commands through JSON and SARIF output on stdout
items.snippet: 0.31.0 fixed GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, where text from a Compose file became GitHub Actions workflow commands in compose-lint's output. `--format json` and `--format sarif` output never passed through that fix, so `##[` inside a service name or other value reaches the log intact when the output is printed to stdout rather than written to a file. The runner acts on `##[` in the middle of a line, so the…
items.summary: Compose-lint can issue CI workflow commands via JSON and SARIF output when untrusted text from pull requests reaches stdout. Upgrade compose-lint to 0.32.0 or later.

The vulnerability exists in versions 19.0.0 through 19.0.8, 19.1.0 through 19.1.9, 19.2.0 through 19.2.8 and 19.3.0 of: - react-serve…
items.summary: A remote code execution vulnerability exists in React Server Components when handling crafted payloads and attacker-controlled values. This affects developers using React Server Components in rare configurations. Upgrade react-server-dom-parcel, react-server-dom-turbopack, and react-server-dom-webpack to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, 19.3.1 or later.
